wizard.title: New Instance
wizard.subtitle: Pick a protocol backend, create the instance, and finish the connection

provider.intro: The backend decides whether NA has to host a protocol container locally. Choose based on your resources and existing setup.

builtin_napcat.description: NA creates and hosts a NapCat container in local Docker. Just scan the QR code to sign in — no protocol backend to set up yourself.

remote_onebot.description: Connect an existing NapCat / LLOneBot / Lagrange OneBot backend. NA only accepts the reverse WebSocket connection.
remote_onebot.cost: No container, zero extra resource cost

native.description: Use a native adapter such as qqbot_openclaw, email, or minecraft to talk to the platform directly, bypassing OneBot.
native.cost: No container, zero extra resource cost

builtin_qbob.description: Connect a QQ official bot through the qbob service bundled with this deployment, which bridges it to OneBot. Scan a QR code or enter the AppID / AppSecret; NA wires it up for you.
builtin_qbob.cost: All bots share one qbob container, roughly 100-200MB RAM
builtin_qbob.unavailable: qbob is not bundled with this deployment (install with --with-qbob)

basic.instanceKeyHint: Lowercase letters, digits and underscores only, up to 32 characters
basic.instanceKeyInvalid: Only lowercase letters, digits and underscores, 1-32 characters
basic.immutableNotice: The instance key is encoded into every chat key and cannot be changed after creation.
basic.adapterHint: Pick the native adapter this instance will use
basic.noNativeAdapter: No native adapter is available. Enable one in adapter management first.

builtin.intro: NA creates and hosts a NapCat container in local Docker. Once it is running, scan the QR code to bring the account online.

create.title: Create container
create.hint: The first run pulls the image and may take several minutes

start.title: Start container
start.hint: The QR code becomes available once the container is running

login.title: Scan to sign in
login.hint: Scan the QR code with your mobile client to sign in

builtin.creatingHint: Working on it — container status refreshes automatically.
builtin.beforeCreate: The container uses roughly 300-500MB RAM on this machine. Make sure Docker is available.
builtin.runningHint: The container is running. You can scan the QR code to sign in now.
builtin.loginDone: Signed in. The instance is connected.

remote.noContainerNotice: This backend creates no container. Just put the connection details below into your existing protocol backend.

guide.open: Open the OneBot configuration page of NapCat / LLOneBot / Lagrange
guide.addWs: Add a reverse WebSocket client and paste the WS URL above
guide.fillToken: Paste the access token above into the auth token field
guide.enable: Save and enable the connection — the backend will connect back to NA

remote.claimHint: Once connected, if the instance shows as unclaimed, claim it from the instance list to bring it under management.

native.intro: The instance is created. Account and credentials for the native adapter are configured on the adapter page.
native.returnHint: Return to the instance list afterwards to check the connection status.

done.title: Instance ready
done.subtitle: Open the instance to check its status and configure channels.

panel.notRunningHint: The container is not running, so the protocol backend cannot connect. Start it first.
panel.emptyDescription: NA will host NapCat in local Docker, using roughly 300-500MB RAM.
panel.emptyNoPermission: No container has been created for this instance yet. Container creation allocates host resources, so ask your service provider to set it up.
panel.remoteNotice: This instance connects to an external protocol backend — NA hosts no container. Put the connection details below into your backend.
panel.nativeNotice: This instance uses the native adapter {{adapter}}. It bypasses OneBot and needs no container; manage its credentials on the adapter config page.
panel.deleteConfirmBody: Container {{name}} will be removed along with its stored login state, so you will need to scan the QR code again. This cannot be undone.

network.title: Network configuration
network.subtitle: A protocol backend can run several connections of different types at once. NekroAgent manages exactly one of them; the rest are yours.
network.restartRequired: Network changes take effect after the container restarts.
network.remoteSyncRequired: After changing the network configuration, update your protocol backend and reconnect.

type.websocketClientsHint: The backend connects out to the given address; this is what NekroAgent uses
type.websocketServersHint: The backend listens on a port and your tools connect in
type.httpServersHint: The backend listens on a port and serves the OneBot HTTP API
type.httpSseServersHint: Same as the HTTP server, but pushes events over SSE
type.httpClientsHint: The backend POSTs events to the given address, which must be a public http/https URL

entry.managedHint: This connection is managed by NekroAgent: its address and token are generated automatically, and it cannot be edited or removed. Only heartbeat, reconnect and debug are adjustable.
entry.name: Connection name
entry.nameHint: Unique per type; letters, digits, underscore, dot and hyphen only
entry.hostHint: Listen address inside the protocol container, usually 0.0.0.0
entry.portHint: Between {{min}} and {{max}}, and must not clash with another connection

errors.duplicateName: Duplicate connection name within the same type: {{name}}
errors.invalidPort: Connection "{{name}}" needs a listen port between {{min}} and {{max}}

login.title: Scan to sign in
login.successHint: The account is signed in. You can close this dialog.
login.boundHint: Account {{account}} is signed in and has been bound to this instance automatically. You can close this dialog.
login.scanHint: Scan the QR code with your mobile client. It refreshes automatically.
login.pollingStopped: Auto refresh stopped. Click "Refresh QR code" to continue.

qbob.intro: Connect a QQ official bot to this instance. NA creates the bot in the bundled qbob, binds the account and wires up the reverse WebSocket; you never need to open qbob's own console.
qbob.serviceUnavailable: The bundled qbob is not available. Check that the qbob container is running.
qbob.attachedHint: Bot {{appid}} is connected, and OneBot account {{selfId}} is bound to this instance.
qbob.groupHint: For the bot to work in a group, the group owner must turn on "proactive messages" and "receive all messages" for it. QQ official bots can only reply within a limited time and number of messages, so proactive messages such as scheduled tasks may fail.
qbob.license: qbob is a separate project licensed under AGPL-3.0, not under this project's license. The image is built locally from the upstream source:

credential.title: Provide a qbob service account
credential.intro: NA needs a qbob admin account to manage bots. If qbob's initial password is no longer available, create an admin account in qbob's console and enter it here.
credential.passwordHint: Write-only; stored encrypted in the NA data directory

connect.scanIntro: Generate a QR code and have the bot owner scan and confirm it in mobile QQ. The bot is connected automatically afterwards.
connect.waitingScan: Waiting for the scan to be confirmed...
connect.pollStopped: Polling stopped after 5 consecutive failures. Regenerate the QR code or try again later.
connect.manualIntro: After creating the bot on the QQ open platform, enter its AppID and AppSecret. The AppSecret is stored only in qbob, never in NA.
connect.appidInvalid: The AppID must be digits only
connect.secretHint: Write-only; it will not be shown again

panel.readOnly: Read-only members cannot view the protocol status.
panel.notAttached: No QQ official bot is connected to this instance yet.
panel.askProvider: Ask your service provider to connect a bot to this instance.
panel.markdown: Enable markdown (needed for real @ in groups)
panel.advancedHint: Advanced features (plugins, groups, message history) live in qbob's own console. It only listens on the host's 127.0.0.1 (port set by QBOB_ADMIN_EXPOSE_PORT in .env, 17810 by default); use an SSH tunnel to reach it remotely.
panel.detachConfirmBody: This deletes bot {{appid}} from qbob and unbinds the account from this instance. The instance itself is kept and can be connected again.
